headline: Finance Committee to review bids for tractor, trailer, airport roof work, CIC boiler, Kenduskeag Stream wall repair, sewer project, and telematics equipment.
summary: The committee will consider purchase and construction bids totaling millions of dollars for Public Works equipment, airport dock roof renovations, a boiler replacement, stream wall repair, sewer flow separation, and vehicle telematics equipment. It will also review a workout agreement renewal for a property on 71 Harvard Street.
items: Compact Tractor purchase from United AG & Turf for $39,081 - Committee Approval
Log Loader Trailer purchase from United AG & Turf for $48,650 - Committee Approval

OTHER COMMENTS:
This work is intended to replace a portion of the Kenduskeag Stream retaining wall located on the south side of 
Hannibal Hamlin Mall Park extending from the Central Street bridge approximately 115 feet east.  The existing wall 
is failing with several blocks becoming dislodged from the toe of the wall in two distinct areas.
The Proposed wall will consist of a modular block wall as presented to the Infrastructure Committee in April of 
2027.  This follows the recommendations presented in the preliminary study completed by DuBois and King, Inc.  
The wall will be designed as part of the contractors services.  Design work is anticipated to commence beginning in 
the fall of 2026 with construction beginning in the winter of 2027 and extending through the end of fall 2027.
The City received three bids for the proposed work.  The City Engineering Department interviewed each of the 
project teams and proposals were graded based on a selection criteria established in the Request for Proposals.  
Based on the grading of the proposals, Gordon Contracting, Inc. was selected as providing the bid that is in the best 
interest of the City.
Gordon's bid was within the established budget for the proposed work and the proposed schedule is acceptable to 
the City.
Staff hereby request approval to enter into a construction contract with Gordon Contracting, Inc. of Sangerville , 
Maine in the amount of $3,871,720 for the design-build work.

Subject: Gordon Contracting Proposed Work Plan 
 
It is Gordon Contracting’s intent to perform the required engineering, design 
and construction for the 125 linear feet of existing retaining wall repair located 
along Kenduskeag Stream as outlined in the report provided by Dubois & King 
as provided by the City of Bangor. Our intent is to remove the existing wall 
materials and replace them with a modular block Redi-Rock wall system with 
grid tie-backs. 
 
EXECUTION 
Our approach will be to partner with Plymouth Engineering located in 
Newport, ME for the initial site survey, permitting and general site design. We 
will also partner with Redi-Rock located in Guilford, ME who will be teamed 
with SW Cole of Hermon, ME for the required wall geotechnical studies and 
ultimate wall design and H.B. Fleming for design/installation of an excavation 
shoring system. Gordon Contracting will perform the general sitework and 
wall installation.
627 N Dexter Road Sangerville, ME 04479 
Office: 207.876.3798 FAX 207.876.3799 
 
KEY PERSONNEL 
Gordon Contracting:  Brian Howard – President 
    Drew Straehle – Project Manager 
    Project Superintendent /Quality Control – TBD 
 
Plymouth Engineering:  Scott Braley, PE 
Redi-Rock:  Tyler Muzzy 
 
Resumes can be provided upon request 
     
PROJECT CHALLENGES/SAFETY CONSIDERATIONS/QUALITY CONTROL 
Some of the initial challenges we face with this project is working with the 
ever-changing water ﬂow, establishing what the in-water window timeframe 
will be (permit driven), excavation support, public safety, access and worker 
safety. Another challenge is ensuring a new modular block wall will ultimately 
“tie-in” with the existing natural blocks.  
Our ﬁrst order of business would be to fence and block pedestrian access to 
the park. There would also be signage installed to notify and direct the public 
around the work area  
We will cofferdam within the stream to create a work area in the dry at the 
base of the wall. This will ensure that our subgrade preparation and concrete 
pour for the footing are completed properly without water ﬂow being an 
impact to the wall. The cofferdam will likely divert the water to the channel on 
the other side of the Park. The installation and design of the cofferdam will be 
driven by what is allowable based on required permits.
627 N Dexter Road Sangerville, ME 04479 
Office: 207.876.3798 FAX 207.876.3799 
 
We will also develop a temporary fall protection system for our workers and 
safety rail for areas that have had existing rail removed for access.  
The site will be equipped with a boat and life safety rings to ensure they are 
available should the need for an in water rescue ever arise. 
Gordon Contracting will provide their safety plan to the city and will be 
followed by our company and all subcontractors 
Redi-Rock is going to customize their blocks to ensure the vertical batter of 
their product falls in line with the batter of the original wall to ensure a proper 
tie-in 
Gordon Contracting will employ an independent testing laboratory for all 
required Quality Control. Our site Superintendent will also ﬁll the role of 
Quality Control Supervisor 
 
INITIAL WORK PLAN/SCHEDULE 
Our anticipated sequence of design and work would be as follows: 
1. Meet with city officials to discuss design intent, pertinent dates, required 
permits, etc. 
2. Design meeting with Plymouth Engineering to discuss plan for initial site 
survey, permit applications, etc. 
3. Meeting with Redi-Rock/SW Cole to discuss initial wall design and 
remaining geotechnical investigation 
4. Meet with H.B. Fleming to discuss design on excavation shoring system 
(their initial approach is a drilled pile system with wood lagging to support 
the required 20-25’ area behind the new wall to a depth of approximately 
26’

OTHER COMMENTS:
This work is intended to lay a portion of the new sewer main along the northeast edge of the property located at 
773 Stillwater extending from Bangor Mall Boulevard to the northeast corner of the Hannaford building.  This new 
main is will eventually be extended trough said parcel to Stillwater Avenue to intercept sewer flow from Stillwater 
Avenue and bring this flow to the Penjajawoc sewer main via gravity flow, therefore bypassing the Kmart pump 
station.  This project is part of a multi phased plan aimed at discontinuing the Kmart Pump Station. 
This phase of the work will remove existing sewer flows from 773 Stillwater, 777 Stillwater and 753 Stillwater from 
the existing Kmart pump station.   This work will remove approximately 9,000 gallons per day from the existing 
pump station, which will free up capacity for other planned developments.  This work is being funded primarily 
through an ARPA Grant awarded to the city for improvements related to the Kmart pump station and surrounding 
sewer network.  A small portion of this work ( approximately 15,000) will be funded through local funds approved 
in the 2027 city budget for work related tot he Kmart pump station.  Due to the ARPA funding source, this work 
must be completed by December 31, 2026, with paving activities being completed by November 25, 2026.
The Engineering Department solicited bids from five qualified contractors who have previously completed work on 
city sewer projects.  The department received bids from three of the contractors.  Of the bids received, C&C Lynch 
Excavation, LLC was the low bidder and can mobilize to the site within 2 weeks of notice to proceed.
Staff hereby request approval to enter into a construction contract with the low bidder, C&C Lynch Excavation, LLC 
of Brewer, Maine in the amount of $454,341.50.

TO: Finance Committee 
FROM: David H. Teelon, Director Public Works 
SUBJECT: Request for Approval - Cooperative Purchase through Maine DOT Sourcewell for 
Procurement with Samsara 
This memo serves to reaffirm and clarify the justification for proceeding with Samsara and 
request contract approval. Samsara’s platform provides critical capabilities for DPW operations, 
including GPS tracking, equipment diagnostics, winter operations monitoring, driver safety tools, 
and regulatory compliance reporting.  
Initial discussion of this procurement occurred previously with Council during the FY27 budget 
workshop; however, several subsequent procedural steps were inadvertently missed. As a 
result, we are now bringing this before Council for potential approval.  
Funding in the amount of $295,968.96 has already been approved in the DPW FY27 Budget. 
This procurement is eligible under Cooperative Purchasing, based on our Procurement Policy, 
through Maine DOT Sourcewell - Contract 102924-SAM, which provides a 
competitively-solicited national cooperative purchasing framework. Use of the Sourcewell 
contract satisfies competitive bidding requirements, supports cost efficiency, and formalizes 
Samsara as an approved vendor under a publicly awarded cooperative contract. 
Conclusion 
Samsara is the only vendor that meets all DPW operational and data‑integration needs. Other 
providers offer fragmented solutions. Therefore, I recommend Committee approval to award a 
three-year contract for the full amount. If approved, a Council Order will appear on the next 
Council agenda. I will be present to answer any questions.
